response.sql:
WITH lab_patients AS (
  SELECT 
    l.ID,
    p.SEX,
    l.PT,
    l.IGA,
    l.IGM,
    CASE WHEN l.IGA IS NOT NULL AND l.IGM IS NOT NULL THEN l.IGA - l.IGM ELSE NULL END AS iga_minus_igm
  FROM Laboratory l
  INNER JOIN Patient p ON l.ID = p.ID
),
patient_averages AS (
  SELECT 
    ID,
    SEX,
    AVG(PT) AS avg_pt,
    AVG(iga_minus_igm) AS avg_iga_minus_igm
  FROM lab_patients
  GROUP BY ID, SEX
),
overall_mean AS (
  SELECT AVG(avg_iga_minus_igm) AS overall_mean_iga_minus_igm
  FROM patient_averages
),
patient_ratios AS (
  SELECT 
    pa.ID,
    pa.SEX,
    pa.avg_pt,
    pa.avg_iga_minus_igm,
    pa.avg_iga_minus_igm / om.overall_mean_iga_minus_igm AS ratio_to_mean
  FROM patient_averages pa
  CROSS JOIN overall_mean om
),
sex_breakdown AS (
  SELECT 
    COALESCE(SEX, '') AS sex,
    AVG(avg_pt) AS avg_patient_pt,
    AVG(avg_iga_minus_igm) AS avg_iga_minus_igm,
    AVG(ratio_to_mean) AS avg_ratio
  FROM patient_ratios
  GROUP BY COALESCE(SEX, '')
)
SELECT * FROM sex_breakdown;

assumptions.assumption: Null and empty string in the SEX column are treated as a single 'blank' group, as the request phrases this as 'keeping patients whose SEX is blank (an empty string) as a separate group'.
The overall mean of IGA-IGM per-patient averages is non-zero; otherwise division by zero occurs in ratio calculation.

alternatives.interpretation: The phrase 'the average of IGA − IGM per record' could mean AVG(IGA) - AVG(IGM) per patient, rather than AVG(IGA - IGM). This averages IGA and IGM separately across records, then subtracts; the primary interpretation computes the difference per record first, then averages.
